summary.headline: Filatex FY26 EBITDA rose 34.5% to INR 346.5 crore on flat volumes, but Q4 FY26 PAT fell 2.75% to INR 40.25 crore amid Middle East-driven crude volatility.
summary.overview: Management compared Q4 FY26 against Q4 FY25 instead of Q3, arguing the sequential comparison was distorted by crude volatility. Q4 revenue was INR 985.5 crore (vs INR 1,080 crore) on 89,841 MT sales, with EBITDA up 13.86% to INR 86.26 crore while PAT fell 2.75% to INR 40.25 crore, partly due to a roughly INR 13 crore forex charge. For FY26, revenue slipped to INR 4,160 crore and volumes were flat, but EBITDA rose 34.5% and PAT rose 36.7%. Management said March was roughly EBITDA-neutral on a current-price basis and that Q1 FY27 utilisation could be 20-25% below the 1 lakh tonne quarterly run rate.

segments.name: Filatex (polyester yarn, core)
segments.commentary: FY26 base polyester margin cited at 8.33%, with Q3 spread around INR 9/kg that compressed sharply in March to roughly EBITDA-neutral. Plant utilisation about 75% vs industry about 60%.

segments.name: Texfil (subsidiary, specialty)
segments.commentary: Management expects EBITDA margin of at least 30% and full-capacity revenue of about INR 350-400 crore from the Ecosis/recycling additions.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 production expected 20-25% below the 1 lakh tonne quarterly level; management declined to forecast beyond the current month.
FY27 revenue estimated at about INR 4,500 crore and FY28 at about INR 4,800 crore for Filatex, plus INR 350-400 crore from the subsidiary.
Steady-state Filatex EBITDA margin targeted at around double digit (11-12% base cited), with PTA localisation adding 1-1.5 percentage points.
Combined capex initiatives expected to add annual EBITDA of INR 218-230 crore; management expects about INR 140 crore total EBITDA uplift in FY27 (INR 70 crore incremental).
Steam distribution project delayed by turbine delivery issue to mid-July 2026; recycling plant targeted for end-September 2026.
FY27 year-end debt estimated at INR 350-360 crore; capex funded from internal accruals, with about INR 335 crore of the INR 690 crore capex as debt.
capex_capacity: Total capex programme of INR 690 crore covering PFY, brownfield expansion, FDY/DTY capacity and higher-margin mix; management says all projects are at an advanced stage of construction.
Textile-to-textile recycling greenfield (about INR 300 crore, 75 tonnes/day chip capacity) targeted to start by end-September 2026; expected top line INR 350-400 crore and EBITDA INR 80-85 crore.
Brownfield expansion expected to add around INR 500 crore top line; total capacity cited near 470,000 MT after the September brownfield addition.
Dahej automation, renewable power expansion and steam distribution to nearby industries (steam project now mid-July).
PTA: GAIL Mangalore expected around July 2026, IOC Paradip around December 2026, Reliance 3.2 million tonnes by end CY2027.
demand_pricing: Demand weak as downstream buyers defer purchases amid high prices; some demand recovery seen from start of May per management.
Petrochemical input costs rose 40-45% amid Strait of Hormuz disruption; manufacturers unable to pass through full cost, compressing yarn and fabric margins.
Post-QCO revocation (November), Chinese imports pressured January-February pricing; management says new Chinese imports will slow as Chinese prices rose, though earlier bookings still arriving.
Indian yarn realisation cited about 10-12% below Chinese realisation; management expects INR 8-12/kg recovery once demand normalises.
Industry utilisation around 60% vs Filatex about 75%. Management says customer raw material inventories are near zero.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q1 FY27 production be sub-optimal given continued volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said output will be 20-25% below the 1 lakh tonne quarterly level at minimum, with further visibility limited given daily changes.

qa_highlights.question: How will forex losses (about INR 13 crore in Q4) be mitigated as PTA self-sufficiency grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will hedge more; full hedging cost is about 3.5-4% per dollar on INR 500-550 crore exposure, i.e. INR 17.5-20 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding structure of the INR 690 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 335 crore is debt and the rest is internal accruals; FY27 year-end debt estimated at INR 350-360 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What ROE is the company targeting?
qa_highlights.answer: ROE reached about 12.96% vs 10.62% earlier, with a further 100-200 bps targeted this year if conditions normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the steam and recycling projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Steam project delayed to mid-July due to a turbine delivery issue; recycling plant on track for end-September with no delay seen. Recycled chip to be sold, with yarn conversion mainly for existing facilities.

qa_highlights.question: Will PTA capacity additions create cost savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there will be negligible savings initially since imports are priced at landed cost; savings expected only once IOC and GAIL capacity creates surplus.

risks_watch: Crude and petrochemical input volatility, and fear of sudden price drop after conflict ends, keeping demand and margins weak; March and current spread close to EBITDA-neutral.
Forex exposure on a largely import-linked raw material base; Q4 forex charge of about INR 13 crore hit PAT, and hedging adds about INR 17.5-20 crore annual cost.
Execution risk: steam project slipped to mid-July; recycling plant (end-September) and new product qualification with global brands (4-6 months approval) may take longer.
Recycling offtake: no client commitment yet; management expects 65-70% utilisation in the first six months.
Chinese imports and labour migration disruptions; management expects the EU FTA to take effect around end CY2026 and remains uncertain on timing.
summary.management_tone: Management was candid about near-term pressure, describing the current quarter as EBITDA-neutral in March and today, and it refused to give firm guidance beyond the current month. It was confident on medium-term structural benefits from PTA localisation, the recycling platform and capex, though several timelines were qualified by terms like "hopefully" and "maybe".

adds.what: Textile-to-textile recycling greenfield, 75 tonnes/day chip capacity (~INR 300 crore)
Brownfield expansion adding ~INR 500 crore top line; total capacity near 470,000 MT after September addition
Steam distribution project to nearby industries (turbine delay)

growth.why: FY27 Filatex revenue guided at ~INR 4,500 crore (about 8% above FY26's INR 4,160 crore), backed by recycling plant (end-Sep 2026) and brownfield additions, but Q1 FY27 output is guided 20-25% below run-rate and demand is weak, so near-term growth is uncertain.
